newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may tender for 70,000t corn/38,000t beans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may tender for 70,000t corn/38,000t beans.

text.p: Falling U.S. soybeans futures prices and the bearish effect of the corn harvest could prompt Taiwan to place up to two tenders for 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said on Monday.
"We expect some tenders to enter soon amid comparatively low U.S. soybeans and corn futures prices," a Mandarin International executive said.
The price of the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) December corn futures contract closed on Friday down 2-3/4 U.S. cents to US$2.75-1/4 a bushel.
U.S.-based traders said on Friday the November contract continued to emit bearish signals although the CBOT November contract was up four cents to end at $7.00-1/2 a bushel.
Taiwan's CK Group of importers would likely tender in the week for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn, traders said. Shipment would be slated for January delivery.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was expected to tender for a combined shipment of 16,000 tonnes corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said. The Hui Shung Group's shipment would be slated for March delivery.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was quoted at T$9.60-$9.80 a kg, down from $9.70-9.90 last week.
The price of corn powders was at $6.95 per kg for Taipei delivery, down from $7.10 a week earlier.
Local Pacific Northwest freight cost was about US$10.50 per tonne and the Gulf of Mexico is about $18.00-$19.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized January and February shipments.
Taiwan's Flour Mills Association would remain on the sidelines this week after it bought two shipments totaling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on October 11, an official said.
The local flour price listed on Friday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier, dealers said.
